top_story.headline: Union PAC tells FEC it received insurance money for "additional misappropriations" of committee funds
top_story.dek: The FEC's October 8 letter to the Seafarers International Union's PAC calls the $13,064.50 receipt related to an apparent unauthorized use of committee funds.
paragraphs: The Seafarers Political Activity Donation - Seafarers International Union of North America (AGLIW) reported a receipt described as "Insurance recovery for additional misappropriations found See memo" totaling $13,064.50 on Schedule A of its September Monthly report (covering August 1-31, 2026). In an RFAI dated October 8 to treasurer Thomas Orzechowski, Jr., the FEC said the receipt "appears to be related to an apparent unauthorized use of Committee funds," and that the Commission may take further legal action while it will consider any clarifying information. The word "additional" suggests earlier misappropriations were found. The response is due November 12, 2026.

Two other RFAIs the same day also cite apparent unauthorized disbursements. The FEC flagged Bish for Congress disbursements described as fraud charges ($483.27 and $1,000.00) and Wells Fargo provisional credits of $5,001.21 and $6,192.30, and asked which expenditures the credits offset. It flagged a $4,767.41 "DISPUTED ACH DEBIT" by the EchoStar Corporation and DISH Network Corporation PAC.

sections.headline: 15 RFAIs and 2 Form 99s from sitting members' campaigns
paragraphs: Fifteen letters from the FEC's Reports Analysis Division went to committees of sitting House members, all dated October 7 or 8 with responses due November 12, 2026. Most are routine: excessive-contribution questions, missing joint-fundraising designations and 48-hour notice gaps. Representative Darrell Issa's committee is the notable one, with post-announcement contributions after he said he would not seek re-election.

items: Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15), committee Torres For Congress: RFAI on the 12-Day Pre-Primary report (filed 10/08) — Two items: contributions that appear to exceed limits (the FEC notes the committee's corrective-action explanation), and PAC contributions above $3,500 from committees that weren't multicandidate committees when they gave (amended pre-primary report). Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Eric Swalwell (D-CA), committee Swalwell For Congress: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (filed 10/08) — Two cash-on-hand adjustment entries on Schedule A noted "Uncashed Checks - See Form 99"; the FEC acknowledges the Form 99 the committee filed July 15 and asks for any further information on the adjustment. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL-8), committee Mike Haridopolos For Congress: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (filed 10/08) — Schedule A shows transfers from Faith, Honor, & Courage that look like joint-fundraising proceeds, but it isn't listed as a joint fundraising representative on the Statement of Organization. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL-8), committee Mike Haridopolos For Congress: RFAI on the 12-Day Pre-Primary report (filed 10/08) — Schedule A shows transfers from Shoring Up Republican Futures Fund (SURF FUND) that look like joint-fundraising proceeds, but it isn't listed as a joint fundraising representative on the Statement of Organization. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Sarah McBride (D-DE-At Large), committee McBride For Delaware Inc.: RFAI on the 12-Day Pre-Primary report (filed 10/08) — Schedule A shows one or more contributions that appear to exceed the per-election limit; the committee may have to refund, redesignate or reattribute them. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-NJ-10), committee Lamonica McIver For Congress: RFAI on the April Quarterly report (filed 10/08) — Contributions appear to exceed limits, and the committee ID given for a contribution from the National Association of Realtors (C70002563) appears to be incorrect (amended report). Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-NJ-10), committee Lamonica McIver For Congress: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (filed 10/08) — Possibly missed 48-hour notices for last-minute contributions; filed 48-hour notices whose contributions don't appear on Schedule A; and two $3,000 last-minute contributions from Joseph W. Kaempfer Jr. on 5/20/2026 were only partly disclosed. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Thomas H. Kean Jr. (R-NJ-7), committee Kean For Congress Inc: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (filed 10/08) — Four items: contributions that appear to exceed limits; contributions received after the 2026 primary but designated for it (allowed only to cover net primary debts); possibly missed 48-hour notices for last-minute contributions; and transfers from LaLota Victory Fund and Patriot Protection Council that look like joint-fundraising proceeds from committees not listed as joint fundraising representatives. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Zach Nunn (R-IA-3), committee Iowans For Zach Nunn: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (filed 10/08) — Four items: contributions that appear to exceed limits (the FEC notes the committee's corrective-action explanation); PAC contributions above $3,500 from committees that weren't yet multicandidate committees when they gave; post-primary contributions designated for the primary; and possibly missed 48-hour notices for last-minute contributions. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Herb Conaway (D-NJ-3), committee Herb Conaway For Congress: RFAI on the April Quarterly report (filed 10/08) — Column B (year-to-date or cycle-to-date) totals on the summary pages don't equal the prior report's Column B plus this report's Column A; an amendment is requested. (Lines 7(a), 7(c), 17 and 22.) Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA-2), committee Troy Carter For Congress: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (filed 10/07) — Payments to credit card companies need memo entries naming the original vendor, date, amount and purpose when a vendor was paid more than $200 in the cycle. Rep. Steve Scalise (R-LA-1), committee Scalise For Congress: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (filed 10/07) — Schedule A refunds don't match contributions previously reported, and conduit contributions lack the original earmarked contributors. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Ron Estes (R-KS-4), committee Ron Estes For Congress: RFAI on the April Quarterly report (filed 10/07) — Schedule A shows one or more contributions that appear to exceed the per-election limit; the committee may have to refund, redesignate or reattribute them. Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA-48), committee Darrell Issa For Congress: RFAI on the April Quarterly report (filed 10/07) — Post-announcement primary contributions must be refunded: the committee kept primary contributions received after the candidate's 3/6/2026 announcement that he wouldn't seek re-election (except to cover net debts), general-election contributions must be returned, and transfers from Grow the Majority look like joint-fundraising proceeds from a committee not listed as a joint fundraising representative. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Adriano Espaillat (D-NY-13), committee Adriano Espaillat For Congress: RFAI on the 12-Day Pre-Primary report (filed 10/07) — Disbursement purposes "Administrative Fees," "March April Consulting Services," "May Consulting Services," "Payment" and "Professional Services" are too vague. Response due 11/12/2026. RFAI letter.

Rep. Lou Correa (D-CA-46), committee Lou Correa for Congress: Form 99 filed 10/09 explaining that, while preparing an amended July 15, 2026 report in response to an FEC information request, the campaign found a cash-on-hand error tied to a contribution misreported in March 2026, forcing amended April 15 and pre-primary reports. Form 99.

Rep. Lou Correa (D-CA-46): second Form 99 filed 10/09 saying three contributions were misreported, which produced apparent excessive contributions on the July 15, 2026 report; the committee says it corrected them so the primary and general elections are reported properly and filed amended reports. Form 99.
Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI-11): the FEC approved termination of her House campaign committee, Haley Stevens for Congress (filed 10/07). Termination approval.

sections.headline: 85 RFAIs to challengers, open-seat candidates, PACs and party committees
paragraphs: The FEC sent another large batch of RFAI letters on October 7 and 8, all with a November 12, 2026 response deadline. Most concern July Quarterly and April Quarterly reports; the most serious involve apparent unauthorized use of committee funds (Seafarers, Bish for Congress and EchoStar), plus negative cash balances, unsigned reports and missing 48-hour notices. Items are listed newest first.

items: Young People For A New Era: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (10/08) — The amended report adds $18,516.17 in disbursements missing from the original, which the committee blamed on a software date-import error; the FEC also says 24-hour reports naming "Don Mickey Designs, Inc" as payee don't match the report's dates. RFAI letter.

U A Local 85 Political Action Committee: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (10/08) — An interest receipt came from "HUNTINGTON BANK" that isn't listed as a committee depository on the Statement of Organization; asked to amend it. Operating expenditures were also put on the wrong summary line. RFAI letter.

The Equity Alliance Fund Action PAC: RFAI on the June Monthly report (10/08) — The report shows voided contributions for independent expenditures totaling $10,860.00 on Schedule A; an uncashed check should instead be a negative entry on Schedule E. RFAI letter.

RFAI letter.

Reviving American Jobs Again PAC DBA Equal Opportunity Now: RFAI on the August Monthly report (10/08) — Contributions received appear to exceed the $5,000 annual limit, and contributions the PAC made to candidates appear to exceed the $5,000 per-election limit. RFAI letter.

RFAI letter.

Oregonians For Common Sense PAC: RFAI on the July Quarterly report (10/08) — The report wasn't signed by the treasurer or designated agent listed on the committee's Statement of Organization; asked to amend with an authorized signature. Other disbursements were also reported on the wrong line. RFAI letter.

RFAI letter.

sections.headline: 16 Form 99 filings, mostly below-threshold statements
paragraphs: Most of the Form 99 letters filed October 8 and 9 are small campaigns telling the FEC they fall under the reporting threshold. Two Emmett White filings carry a 22-page loan packet, and a plumbers' union filed a $899,682 independent-expenditure report on paper (two further Form 99s from Representative Lou Correa are under Sitting Lawmakers).

items: EDF Action Votes (PAC, filed 10/09): Letter answering an FEC request dated October 7, saying it amended Schedule E of the August Monthly report to add detail to an independent-expenditure description. Form 99.
Debt Relief PAC (PAC, filed 10/09): Says it filed an amended June 2026 Monthly report on 10/09 fixing the errors cited in an August 6, 2026 RFAI. Form 99.

Ronald Huffman for Congress Election Committee (House candidate, filed 10/08): Candidate letter saying he lost the California 25th District primary, says he spent about $17,000 on the campaign though earlier statements were each under $5,000, and asks the FEC to correct its records; no amended report was attached. Form 99.

Emmett White (PAC, committee ID C00880609, filed 10/09): Filed as a "C-1/Loan Agreement" Form 99, but the 22-page document is a Form 3X report template with the name "Hope Community Shelter" and a 08/15–09/30/2026 coverage period; most filled-in figures could not be read from the extracted text, and the filer's address matches the next entry. Form 99.

Emmett Lee White (presidential committee, committee ID C00931535, filed 10/09): The same 22-page "C-1/Loan Agreement" packet under a second committee ID, signed by treasurer Emmett Lee White at the same Indianapolis address; the same treasurer is behind both filings. Form 99.

Jasmine Hull for President (presidential candidate, filed 10/09): Says it has not crossed the reporting threshold as of October 9, 2026, and notes a $100 candidate loan received September 14, 2026. Form 99.

Luis Galvan for Congress (House candidate, filed 10/09): Says that as of September 30, 2026 it had not received contributions or made expenditures over $5,000, so no October Quarterly report is required. Form 99.
Luis Galvan for Congress (filed 10/09): A second, word-for-word identical statement filed the same day. Form 99.
Raul Ivhan Cortina for President (presidential candidate, filed 10/09): States the committee has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold. Form 99.
Rampke for President (presidential candidate, filed 10/09): Says it did not receive any donations. Form 99.
Ellsworth for President (presidential candidate, filed 10/08): Says the campaign is waiting until after the midterms to raise money and has neither raised nor spent more than $5,000. Form 99.
Committee to Elect Charlotte Magoon (House candidate, filed 10/09): Statement for the public record that it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold. Form 99.
Christopher Dennison for Congress (House candidate, filed 10/09): Says it has not taken in more than $5,000 in donations. Form 99.
Common Sense for America (PAC, filed 10/09): Says it has not reached the threshold and has had zero activity. Form 99.
Morrison for Congress (House candidate, filed 10/08): Says no funds have been raised. Form 99.

United Association of Journeymen and Apprentices of the Plumbing and Pipe Fitting Industry (non-committee filer, paper filing received 10/08): Form 5 independent-expenditure report totaling $899,682.00, all paid to Nuckels Media Partners, Inc on 10/07: $599,138.00 for a digital and radio ad described as supporting Sherrod Brown for U.S. Senate in Ohio, $150,272.00 for a digital ad described as supporting Brian Fitzpatrick in Pennsylvania's 1st District, and $150,272.00 for a digital ad described as supporting Rebecca Bennett in New Jersey's 7th District. Form 99.

sections.headline: One Transaction Reversal: $13,791 Investment Loss
paragraphs: One financial transaction with a negative amount of $10,000 or more was filed this week. In FEC records, large negative amounts represent voided, reversed, or refunded transactions—typically routine corrections to prior filings, though they occasionally mark the unwinding of a transaction after unexpected circumstances.

items: JULIA BROWNLEY FOR CONGRESS: $13,791.20 to Wells Fargo & Co., reported September 30, 2026, described as an unrealized investment account loss.
